article.title: How to make a PowerPoint with AI in taqreer.ai
article.intro: A professional presentation used to take hours of writing, formatting, and picking colors. With taqreer.ai you write your idea or upload a file, and the AI designs a complete PowerPoint deck with slides built for their content, in Arabic and English, which you then edit and export. That is what sets it apart from ready-made templates: every slide is designed fresh around your content.

sections.heading: How to create a presentation with AI

steps: Write your topic or paste your content, or upload a PDF, PowerPoint, or Word file.
Choose your brand, or leave colors on auto so the AI picks a palette that fits the topic.
Set the size (16:9 or 9:16) and slide count, and pick a design style and slide numbering if you want them.
Check the credit cost before you start, then click create and watch the slides appear one by one.
Adjust anything in the [editor](/powerpoint-online), then export to PowerPoint, PDF, or [other formats](/export).

sections.heading: How to write a brief that gets a better deck

bullets: The audience: company management, new clients, or high school students.
The goal: to persuade, to explain a plan, or to present results.
The key points and numbers that must appear in the deck.
The language you want the deck in, Arabic or English.

sections.heading: What makes PowerPoint AI in taqreer.ai different?

bullets: A design for every slide: the AI picks each slide's layout for its content instead of pouring text into one fixed template.
Built-in review: after generating, the AI checks the slides and improves any with layout, overflow, or readability problems.
Arabic-first: right-to-left direction that stays correct even in the PowerPoint file. See [Arabic presentations](/arabic-presentations).
Images that fit: the AI can add [generated images](/powerpoint-images) to any deck, free on your trial.

sections.heading: A clear credit cost
blocks: Each deck uses credits based on its slide count and the generation quality you choose, and you see the cost before you start. article.title: Arabic PowerPoint without text direction problems
article.intro: Anyone who has designed an Arabic deck knows the problem: the text looks fine in the design tool, then it opens in PowerPoint with flipped alignment, English words and numbers scrambled inside sentences, and lines breaking in odd places. taqreer.ai was built Arabic-first, so it handles these problems both in the design and in the exported PowerPoint file.

sections.heading: Why does Arabic text break in PowerPoint?
blocks: Arabic runs right to left, while English words and numbers run left to right. When both directions share a line, the PowerPoint file needs the right direction settings for every paragraph and text box. Many English-first tools don't set all of these, so the deck looks fine in the browser and breaks after export.

sections.heading: How taqreer.ai keeps Arabic right

bullets: Correct direction and alignment for every Arabic paragraph in the exported PowerPoint.
English words and numbers in their correct place inside Arabic sentences.
Line-width correction so Arabic text does not wrap differently when the file opens in PowerPoint.
Your own Arabic fonts are embedded in the exported file when you upload them to your [brand kit](/brand-kit).
Control the direction of each text box in the [editor](/powerpoint-online), for decks that mix Arabic and English.

sections.heading: Common mistakes in Arabic presentations

bullets: Left-aligned Arabic text, which makes a deck look translated rather than designed in Arabic.
Punctuation at the wrong end of the sentence because of the paragraph direction.
A font without good Arabic support, so letters appear disconnected or in a fallback font.
Lists and bullets that start on the left while the text reads from the right.

blocks: In taqreer.ai, Arabic slides are designed right to left from the start, so you don't have to fix these mistakes by hand after every deck.

sections.heading: Arabic fonts for presentations
blocks: The font is one of the biggest signs of a professional Arabic deck. Pick a font that supports Arabic in all its weights, and use a bold weight for headings and a regular weight for body text. If your brand has its own fonts, upload them once to your brand kit so they are used in every deck and embedded in the PowerPoint file, and the deck shows your font even on a computer that doesn't have it.

swiss.does: Lays every slide on a visible column grid with thin rules, off-centre blocks and one small accent colour. Clean, precise and very organised.
swiss.best: Architecture, design, engineering, research and tech talks.

corporate.does: Each slide opens with its main conclusion as the title, then backs it with stat boxes, tables and clean charts. Colours carry meaning (up, down, neutral).
corporate.best: Quarterly reports, financials, KPIs, board meetings and consulting.

minimal.does: One idea per slide: a single big number, word or photo fills most of the slide, with lots of empty space around it.
minimal.best: Product launches, keynote talks, vision decks and inspiring speeches.

editorial.does: A magazine layout with a tinted side column and a main column, small labels above headings and thin rules between blocks. Photos carry the colour.
editorial.best: Case studies, culture, history, journalism and annual reports.

bold.does: Giant headlines on full brand-colour backgrounds, running off one edge of the slide. Loud, confident and impossible to miss.
bold.best: Marketing campaigns, brand launches, pitch openers and events.

duotone.does: Every slide is a full-screen photo (or a two-colour split) with bold text over a dark gradient so it stays readable.
duotone.best: Tourism, events, sports, real estate and storytelling.

playful.does: Rounded cards in bright colours with hard drop shadows and a repeated circle or blob shape. Fun, friendly and energetic.
playful.best: Kids, training, social media, consumer apps and HR.

brutalist.does: Thick borders box every area, with heavy flat colour blocks, no rounded corners and no gradients. Raw and striking.
brutalist.best: Startups, creative agencies, fashion and edgy tech.

classroom.does: Built for teaching: numbered steps, key-idea boxes, definition cards and simple labelled diagrams, with text large enough to read from the back of a class.
classroom.best: Lessons, school projects, training courses, workshops and lectures.

official.does: A formal institutional look: a solid header band, numbered sections, ruled tables and labelled figures. Restrained, symmetric and authoritative.
official.best: Ministry and government reports, strategy plans, compliance and official briefings.

heritage.does: Arabic and Islamic heritage: geometric star patterns as borders and ornaments, arch-shaped frames and balanced, symmetric layouts.
heritage.best: Ramadan and Eid, national days, culture, tourism and heritage topics.

luxury.does: Quiet luxury on a near-black background: thin fine frames, lots of empty space and elegant light headlines. One focal element per slide.
luxury.best: Real estate, perfume, jewellery, hospitality and premium brands.

techglass.does: A dark background with soft glowing colours and frosted-glass cards holding the content. Modern and futuristic.
techglass.best: AI, software, fintech, cybersecurity and product demos.

startup.does: A clean modern pitch: bold headlines with one highlighted word, soft rounded cards, pill tags and simple line icons.
startup.best: Investor pitches, product features, company profiles and team updates.

infographic.does: Turns points into visuals: icons with numbers, process arrows, timelines and simple charts, with very little paragraph text.
infographic.best: Processes, statistics, awareness campaigns, how-to guides and summaries.

sketch.does: A warm notebook feel: paper-like background, doodled underlines, circled words, hand-drawn arrows and highlighter marks.
sketch.best: Brainstorms, workshops, kids' lessons, ideas and creative talks.

organic.does: Calm and natural: earthy colours, soft blob shapes, rounded photo frames and plenty of breathing room.
organic.best: Wellness, health, sustainability, food, beauty and agriculture.

retro.does: A nostalgic print look: warm muted colours, chunky rounded headlines, sunburst and stripe motifs, badges and a light paper grain.
retro.best: Cafes and restaurants, events, branding stories and creative talks.

collage.does: A creative scrapbook: overlapping photo frames, slightly tilted, with tape strips, sticker labels and layered cards.
collage.best: Travel, events recaps, student projects, moodboards and social stories.

earlyyears.does: Made for ages 4 to 7: one idea per slide, a single big word or short phrase, cheerful colours, rounded shapes and friendly cartoon pictures that carry the meaning.
earlyyears.best: Kindergarten, grades 1 and 2, letters and numbers, colours, animals, songs and simple stories.

university.best: University lectures, seminars, thesis and research presentations, and academic conferences.

faq.q: What is taqreer.ai?
faq.a: taqreer.ai is an AI platform that turns your content, text, a file, or an idea, into a fully designed professional presentation in Arabic and English within minutes.

faq.q: How do I design a presentation with AI?
faq.a: Write your topic or upload a file in taqreer.ai, choose your brand, and the AI designs a complete presentation in minutes that you can edit and export to PowerPoint.

faq.q: Does taqreer.ai design presentations and reports in Arabic?
faq.a: Yes. taqreer.ai is Arabic-first with full right-to-left support and Arabic fonts, and it turns your ideas and files into designed presentations and reports in Arabic and English.

faq.q: Does it fully support Arabic?
faq.a: Yes. taqreer.ai is Arabic-first: correct RTL direction, elegant Arabic fonts, and bidirectional formatting that handles English words and numbers inside Arabic text accurately.

faq.q: How does the credit system work?
faq.a: Each deck uses credits based on its slide count and the model used. You get monthly credits with your plan, plus {credits} free credits at signup to try the platform.

faq.q: Can I edit the deck after creating it?
faq.a: Absolutely. The editor lets you edit text, colors, and slides and reorder them, with autosave and checkpoints you can revert to anytime.

faq.q: Can I export the deck to PowerPoint?
faq.a: Yes. You export your decks as an editable PPTX for PowerPoint on every plan, with the Arabic formatting and text direction preserved.

faq.q: Can I apply my own brand identity?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your logo, colors, and fonts in the brand identity section, and taqreer.ai applies them automatically so your decks stay on-brand.

faq.q: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?
faq.a: Yes. You can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel anytime from your account settings, with no long-term commitment.
